title: Apply parallel worker memory budgets on Windows
head: ddd8690874ecab0eea671d4c68de8bbb3ed8b991
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Native Windows has no `os.sysconf`, so `run_parallel.memory_gib()` returned `None` and the default worker count ignored the documented three-GiB-per-worker budget. On the tested Windows host, the old code chose 32 workers; querying 31.297 GiB of physical RAM now selects 10. The shared `verify_parallel.default_jobs()` also receives the detected capacity.

Use the standard-library `ctypes` binding to `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`, with the SDK's fixed-width fields and initialized structure length. Preserve the POSIX query, explicit `JOBS` overrides and unknown-memory fallback. This restores the existing **total physical memory heuristic**; it is not a free-memory reservation or a hard resource limit. No scientific input, certificate, selected result or kappa changes.

## Validation

The new tests produced **five failures against the unchanged base implementation**. After the fix:

| Environment | Check | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows, CPython 3.12.9 | `python -X utf8 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_parallel_memory.py -v` | 11 pass, including the real Windows API |
| Windows, CPython 3.14.2 | Same command | 11 pass |
| Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL, CPython 3.12.3 | `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_parallel*.py' -v` | 17 tests, one Windows-only smoke test skipped; all others pass |

Controls cover a fractional capacity above 4 GiB, total versus available memory, API failure with a populated buffer, zero/unknown capacity, CPU and minimum-worker bounds, explicit overrides, and the shared isolated-group budget. The existing Windows-safe scheduler tests also pass (four tests covering overrides, failure propagation, snapshots and invalid CLI/group inputs).

`python -X utf8 -B scripts/research_baseline.py`, `python -X utf8 -B scripts/verify_selected_result.py` and `git diff --check` pass. The source-bound baseline reports the unchanged selected record. No heavy audit workers were launched for the scheduler comparison. Full historical/mathematical replay was not run for this tooling-only change. Hosted CI is separate from these local results.

Hosted CI currently requires maintainer approval: [Verify research artifacts](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38610219719) reports `action_required` with no jobs executed. The local results above do not claim hosted CI success.

## Credit

Retain the existing Apache-2.0 notice and credit eumemic's PR154 worker policy and the integrated maintenance work. API layout and return semantics follow Microsoft's [MEMORYSTATUSEX](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/ns-sysinfoapi-memorystatusex) and [GlobalMemoryStatusEx](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-globalmemorystatusex) documentation. Prepared for Tairitsu-Aya with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

## Open next questions

This is an existing-tool repair, not a new research package. Accounting for competing processes, free RAM or container/job-object limits would require a separate scheduling-policy change; this patch preserves the current total-memory policy.
